Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) G.notes: Committee revived in 2024 after two dormant years; won a state tourism award Oct 2025. Latest full cycle documented is the Nov 21, 2025 approvals ($81,000, 15 awards, for events Jan-Jun 2026). The Apr 2026 cycle (events Jul 2026-Jun 2027) is only partly documented: Apr 15, 2026 minutes list 7 approvals, five without amounts, and the Apr 29, 2026 special-meeting minutes with the remaining recommendations were not retrievable. Press reporting on the Nov 2025 round said about 28 applications and roughly $86,000 with a $1,000-per-awardee marketing contingency. Committee discussed conflict-of-interest issues with member organizations applying (Jul 2026 agenda). Visit Spokane's TPA page now directs event organizers to TACI.

Spokane Sports Community Grant.typical_award: Requests up to $10,000 across event support, equipment loan and marketing; marketing support capped at $3,000 per event. Hotel support is discounted-rate booking via EventConnect rather than cash.
Spokane Sports Community Grant.notes: Spokane Sports does not publish a recipient list and no press coverage naming community-grant awardees was found. Program is for tournaments/competitions that generate overnight stays; local nonprofits and for-profits eligible; cash match encouraged but not required. Spokane Sports is itself funded by TPA (e.g., $700,000 from the Spokane Valley 2026 TPA budget). Recipient data would need to be requested directly from Spokane Sports.

Spokane Arts Grant Awards (SAGA).typical_award: Requests up to $10,000; round pools of about $50,000 to $60,000 funding 6-8 projects, so typical awards run roughly $5,000 to $10,000. Annual total $166,000 (2025 and 2026). Three rounds per year.

Spokane County Tourism Promotion Area (T.notes: The Spokane County TPA Commission (administered through Visit Spokane) has 'opted to hold on Event Grants through 2027' and directs event and festival organizers to the City of Spokane TACI grant instead. TPA revenue ($5 per room night) funds Visit Spokane and Spokane Sports contracts. No recipient list for prior TPA event grants was found online. The City of Spokane Valley runs its own TPA ($1.77M 2026 budget: $875,000 to 116 & West for destination marketing, $700,000 to Spokane Sports, $170,000 Opportunity Fund); no Opportunity Fund awardees published yet.

4Culture Projects grants.typical_award: Art Projects: fixed request tiers of $2,500, $5,000, $7,500, $10,000, $12,500 or $15,000 (plus possible Equity Investment add-on). Heritage Projects: similar project-grant scale. Open 4Culture: up to $2,500, rolling. Historical benchmark: 2018 Projects round funded 196 projects totaling $1,076,996 from 441 applications.

Partnership in Economic Development Prog.notes: cdrpa.org was not fetchable (not on allowlist); program page at ccpd.com describes it as an opportunity fund (nonprofit track and municipality track) with no deadline and no published recipient list. In Feb 2024 commissioners moved to tighten event funding: applicants must show attendees from outside Chelan/Douglas counties, port money covers event deficits only, and the program would shift away from tourism toward living-wage jobs and private investment. Amounts above come from news reports, not an official list; 2025 year for YMCA/Pybus is inferred.

Historical Promotion Grants.notes: The county has not posted award announcements for the 2024, 2025 or 2026 cycles; the most recent published list is the 2020 cycle (announced Dec 30, 2019). Program was suspended in 2021 per page metadata and later resumed. Eligibility is limited to nonprofits/public entities that operate a museum or similar institution or conduct heritage education/interpretation in Clark County; an event qualifies only with a local-history interpretation angle. Recent awardee lists would require a records request to historicpreservation@clark.wa.gov or review of Clark County Council consent agendas in November/December.

Cowlitz County Tourism Grant (Lodging Ta.notes: Cowlitz County Tourism (visitmtsthelens.com, Tourism Director Kim Boccuti, 360-577-3137) runs two tracks: an annual Tourism Marketing/Small Grant for events (applications due early November; $50,000 pool for 2026) and a Large Grant for infrastructure and major projects (applications due Mar 25, 2026; up to $200,000, projects within two years, must draw visitors from beyond 50 miles). Olympic Peninsula Visitor Bureau Tourism.typical_award: Usually up to $7,500 per project/event and up to $15,000 per organization per year; partial funding common. Annual pool about $125,000 (2025). Priority to events marketed off the Peninsula, in unincorporated Clallam County, in the mid-October to May 31 shoulder season, lasting two or more days and generating lodging.
Olympic Peninsula Visitor Bureau Tourism.notes: Now branded the Clallam County Tourism Enhancement Grant, administered by OPVB and funded by unincorporated Clallam County lodging tax (RCW 67.28.1816). OPVB does not publish award lists; the only recipient coverage found was a 2014 Sequim Gazette item ($17,650 awarded that round). Large events and infrastructure are referred to the Clallam County LTAC instead. Advertising inside Clallam/Jefferson counties is capped at 25% of the award; OPVB logo and OlympicPeninsula.org link required on materials; final report within 45 days with room-night data. Contact OPVB at 360-452-8552 for prior awardees.
